thread.title: Buy Netflix And Chill, It's Going Back To $400 - Part 2 - Netflix, Inc. (NASDAQ:NFLX)

author: Dan Victor, CFA
title: Buy Netflix And Chill, It's Going Back To $400 - Part 2 - Netflix, Inc. (NASDAQ:NFLX)
text:
Netflix, Inc. ( NFLX ) ended a volatile 2018 up an impressive 40% on the year despite a near 35% pullback from its all-time high of $423 set last summer. The stock came under pressure following both its Q2 and Q3 earnings releases on concerns regarding the company's heavy content spending and recurring negative free cash flow. I view Netflix as a "top pick" for 2019 with the recent weakness among the broader market sell-off as a buying opportunity. Looking ahead to Q4 earnings set to be released January 17, Netflix can beat expectations with strong subscriber growth which could be a near-term upside catalyst. I have a 2019 price target of $400 representing 50% upside.
Netflix stock chart. source - finviz.com
The numbers here are really impressive and if anything, the current brand momentum has only strengthened in recent months reaffirming the bullish case I laid out in a previous article, Buy Netflix and Chill - It's Going Back to $400 published November 1, 2018. This update presents new information and addresses some questions posed by readers in the comments section.
No other company has this type of growth and potential Fellow contributor Williams Bay Analytics amicably took me to task in the comment section for proclaiming "No other company has this type of growth and potential" when referring to Netflix. He says;
Really? How many listed stocks are there? How do you know that NFLX is better than all of them based on growth and potential?
Netflix to me really is a unique stock and I stand by that statement. The way I can quantify my opinion is by running a stock screen to find alternative tickers with similar attributes. I set the following filter:
Market cap above $10bn (universe of large-cap stocks) Revenues above $5bn Positive profit margin last quarter (profitable companies) Consensus double-digit revenue growth each of next 3 years 2018 consensus EPS growth > 100% 2019-2020 consensus EPS average > 10% According to the YCharts database, 15 stocks match these criteria. Netflix just happens to have the highest consensus revenue and EPS growth over the next three years among large-cap stocks.
Stock screen results. Source - data by YCharts , author compilation
Street estimates are looking for Netflix to grow revenues 35.3% for the fiscal year 2018, 25.8% for 2019, and 22.7% for 2020. Within the group of stocks with similar levels of expected revenue growth, Vertex Pharmaceuticals ( VRTX ), Salesforce.com ( CRM ), Amazon ( AMZN ), and Alphabet, Inc. ( GOOGL ) (NASDAQ: GOOG ) round out the top five in terms of consensus revenue growth.
Stock screen results. Source - data by YCharts , author compilation
Within the same screen results sorted by 2-fiscal-year ahead EPS estimates, consensus data shows Netflix may grow earnings from $1.25 per share last year in 2017 to $6.58 by 2020. Over the next 2-year period between 2019 and 2020, Netflix is expected to grow EPS more than any other stock in the group. In terms of P/E multiple, Netflix is among the most "richly priced" of the group trading at 65x forward earnings, but I believe this type of growth premium is justified. Netflix is on track to double revenues to $30 billion by 2021 and even then should still be able to grow revenues above 20% that year. I believe the bullish case for the stock represents upside to revenue and earnings beyond consensus.
Back to addressing the comment by Williams Bay Analytics, he's right that there's no way of knowing if Netflix is better than all the others. My point is that Netflix belongs to a very select group of mega-cap growth stocks. Of course, expected growth alone does not make Netflix or any other stock a good investment, but it's a good starting point to examine further. In this case, there is much more to the story.
The Bullish Case A major milestone in 2018 was that the international segment for the first time overtook the domestic market as the larger half of revenue. Netflix is set to end 2018 with about 139 million subscribers worldwide and I view this climbing to 500 million over the next decade. The growth is being propelled by the international markets with subscriber growth near 40% this year against 10.5% domestically. My long-term subscriber and revenue forecast introduced in my original article is reproduced below.
Netflix, Inc. Revenue Model. Source: Historical from Netflix / author forecasts
Summarizing the points detailed previously, in essence, I believe the market is underestimating Netflix's international growth potential and isn't giving the company credit for unexploited pricing power.
Still early stage of growth
I estimate that Netflix can reach 500 million total paid subscribers by 2028, up 3.6x from the current levels. Low market penetration internationally
Market penetration in the US is currently about 55% and 13% internationally (ex. China), based on households with a broadband internet connection as the addressable market. Over the next 10 years, U.S. penetration will reach around 75% of broadband households while the International market will approach 40%. Some developed markets should be able to approach the same level of penetration, in my opinion. Netflix is just beginning to produce foreign language original programming.
This is the secret sauce. I'm really bullish on the steps Netflix is taking to expand foreign language originals. From 1 show in 2015 to 19 that premiered in 2018; Netflix is enticing viewers internationally with localized content. The hope for investors here is that Netflix can 'strike gold' with a mega hit in a country like India that drives market penetration to converge with the US. In Brazil, for example, the show "The Mechanism" became must-watch TV according to reports that likely added to Netflix's momentum in the country. Rivals in the streaming game including Disney ( DIS ) and Time Warner (NYSE: TWX ) have yet to enter the foreign language content space and this represents a major advantage to Netflix in the international market.
Netflix, Inc. Foreign Language TV Shows. Source: adapted from Wikipedia
Unexploited Pricing Power
$10.99 for basic plan in the US is a good value compared to rival HBO Now at $14.99 In Q3 the average subscriber in the U.S. paid $11.34 per month (based on different tiers) and $8.95 internationally. The Tech consulting firm CompariTech has a report that highlights the different prices Netflix charges by country . In summary, the monthly rate in USD varies from a low $3.27 in Turkey, $5.80 a month in Japan to as high $12.37 in Denmark. I predict a price hike of $2 for 2020 to $12.99 for the most popular plan in the US. Over the next decade, US consumers could be paying $19.99 or more depending on how Netflix chooses to move forward with monetization. Concerns of Negative Free Cash Flow are overstated
Netflix is guiding for negative free cash flow of $3 billion for the full year 2018 and 2019, driven by $13 billion of content spending on a cash basis and $8 billion on an amortized basis. By my calculation, $3 billion in negative free cash flow for 2019 translates to about $1.45 per 2019 global subscriber, or $3.91 just for 2019 forecast U.S. subscribers. Netflix could simply hike the price of its most popular monthly plan to $14.99 in the U.S. tomorrow and be cash-flow neutral. New Revenue Opportunities My $71.1-billion dollar revenue forecast by 2028 considers only subscriber growth and a gradual average price hike over the next decade. The reality is that Netflix can go beyond this forecast with the potential to branch out into a number of new growth opportunities beyond streaming. Two immediate considerations are advertising and movie-theater releases.
Movie Theaters
Netflix could premiere an expected big-hit in theaters maybe for a limited run before releasing it on the streaming service. I think subscribers would be okay with this approach with the understanding that some action and visually grand films are best seen on the big-screen; even appreciating the opportunity. The demand for the movie theater experience is not going away, so Netflix could and should embrace it. Company has already shown a film in theaters with the critically acclaimed 'Roma' in a limited run to qualify for Oscar consideration so the concept is not new. The recent film 'Bird Box' is an example that likely could have been a massive box office hit with a worldwide first run theater distribution. I estimate the movie could have attained $300 million plus at the box office worldwide. (discussed more below). Consider the possibility of a 'Stranger Things' movie launching in theaters. Netflix may be on the cusp of rivaling major studios with record breaking "blockbusters." The prospect of a-billion dollar franchise launching from Netflix in the coming years is very real, in my opinion. Advertising
The Netflix platform and data have the potential to be a very powerful advertising tool should Netflix attempt to go in that direction. Ads could be localized to cities around the world and targeted for different demographics. A simple example could be a local restaurant pays Netflix to show a clip before a cooking show. Concept could be developed from simple static "tiles" across selection menu or interactive "overlays" during opening credits. Discreet or not. Could provide flexibility for future pricing tiers of the service, example charge more for premium 4k streaming package with no ads or keep a lower price basic plan with ads. I'm sure Reed Hastings and his team will figure it out. Bird Box Highlights Value Proposition and Pricing Power 'Bird Box' promotional image. -Netflix
Netflix released the original movie ' Bird Box ' starring Sandra Bullock December 21, later announcing that it broke records for viewership on the site. Netflix said the film was viewed by 45 million accounts in its first seven days. The movie has become a major hit for Netflix drawing strong reviews and pop culture references . The seemingly out-of-nowhere success of Bird Box highlights Netflix's unique position of consistently leading with content that is able to draw viewers.
I watched Bird Box over the holidays and felt it would have likely been a major "box-office" hit if it was released in theaters. In fact, the 2018 movie 'A Quiet Place ' distributed by Paramount Pictures, a Viacom company ( VIAB ) provides great comparable data. Both movies curiously follow the same post-apocalyptic horror-thriller premise. In A Quiet Place, a family must not make sounds and remain quiet to avoid detection by extraterrestrial invaders. In Bird Box, a group of characters must not make eye-contact with a mysterious force to remain alive.
'A Quiet Place' movie poster. Source- Wikipedia
Apparently, the play-on-senses has been a hit with audiences because 'A Quiet Place' achieved a worldwide box office total of $340 million ($188 million domestically) with a production budget of $17 million. I suspect Bird Box would have achieved similar numbers or better if it had been released in theaters. Netflix instead chose to simply add to its value proposition by premiering the film on its streaming service. Overall, I think it was the right decision to keep it on the streaming service this time and not go to theaters. Netflix is still in the early stage of its experimentation and learning phase and the success of Bird Box will be taken into consideration for future feature. In context, my estimated $340 million figure would have only added about 2.1% to 2018 revenues, but the real impact is the positive perception Netflix receives by customers when assessing renewal of the service leading to lower churn. The quality of Netflix earnings will only improve with an ever larger subscriber base. I believe Netflix is largely immune to current concerns about economic growth that has led to broad market volatility. The growth story is very much intact.
Back to Valuation - Show me the DCF Fellow Contributor Long-Short Manager made a great point in the comment section of the previous article.
How do you *know* that 100x PE or 40x 2 yr fwd PE is rich, fair or cheap? A DCF is the only way I know. If you have a table and an explanation for how you know, I think many of us would be interested.
It's true that DCF models are a great way to measure intrinsic value but I don't find them that useful for stocks like Netflix that are in a high growth stage with negative free cash flow. There are just too many variables to forecast. Nevertheless, in the name of research, I was able to put together some numbers that demonstrate a valuation path to $400. Take it with a grain of salt.
Netflix can be free cash flow positive in 3 years when revenues approach $30 billion, nearly double the current level. The big unknown to forecast free cash flow for Netflix is how much content spending the company will produce out into the future. My underlying assumption is that content spending will not, nor does not need to grow linearly with subscribers or new markets. Netflix is adding content, yes, but I view the current base of programming as supporting a higher subscriber level worldwide. The number of subscribers for the same program catalog will simply increase.
My expectation is that revenue growth will greatly outpace content spending over the next decade. Netflix is set to spend about $13 billion in 2018 on content on a cash basis, let us assume doubles to ~$26 billion in 10 years. The key here is that revenues at that time would be 3x content spending according to my model in 2028, up from ~1.2x currently. Keep in mind that Netflix is also becoming more "profitable" in terms of margins. Q3 profit margin reached 10% while EBITDA margin reached 12.72% for Q3 and 11.3% for the trailing twelve months. Free cash flow will accelerate quickly once content spending levels off.
NFLX Profit Margin [ TTM] data by YCharts
DCF
My goal here is to provide a reference point to further the discussion. The model could be further refined but the core insight is that free cash flow could reach $15 billion per year over the next decade.
Starting point is subscribers reaching 500 million in 2028 with revenue of $71.1bn as per the model previously shared. Q3 TTM EBITDA margin reached 11.3% and this is expected to accelerate going forward leading to free cash flow in the future. My model has EBITDA margin at 30% by 2028 comparable to what Disney reports now. For Netflix, when we think of content spending the number is not considered "capex" but actually an amortized expense recorded as a cost of revenue "COGS" essentially working capital. Actual capex is only the traditional net additions of PPE like a corporate office building. To calculate free cash flow, one needs to forecast the content spending out 10 years which admittedly is pure speculation. $26 billion in content in 10 years is double the 2018 level. For reference, Disney/Fox is reported to have a current spend of $22 billion this year on original and acquired content.
Netflix discounted cash flow model. Source - author estimates
I'll admit that there was some data-fitting here to meet the $400 price level but this is simply my base-case scenario, the bullish case has upside. The revenue starting point for this model only includes subscriber growth and gradual price hikes. There is a strong likelihood Netflix introduces a new revenue stream over the next decade like advertisements. Potential M&A down the line is also a possibility. All DCF models are highly sensitive to inputs, particularly the long-term growth estimate and cost of capital. In this case, a 50bps revision to either the WACC or terminal growth rate alters the price by approximately $30 per share.
P/E Mulitple An anonymous reader poked fun at a statement I made in the previous article when I described Netflix's current valuation.
On a trailing P/E basis, Netflix is trading at 100x earnings which is the cheapest since Q1 2015." This may be one of the funniest sentences I've ever read in my life. - 984591
I agree that cheap in the same sentence as 100x earnings may not the best choice of words. The reader was right because Netflix which was trading at $275 at the time went on to fall further to a low of $232 by late December. Still, my feeling is that if any stock in the market deserves this type of premium, give it to Netflix. My case is that the growth outlook for Netflix has only strengthened in the period it last traded at the current multiple level and deserves a richer valuation from here. The combination of brand momentum, expected growth, pricing power, and new monetization opportunities present a compelling case. The price target of $400 represents 100x 2019 consensus earnings.
NFLX data by YCharts
Takeaway As I'm publishing this article the latest headline to jolt the market is Apple ( AAPL ) cutting revenue guidance amid poor China sales while blaming the US-China trade dispute. It is encouraging to note that Netflix has little exposure to China other than licensing deals as it does not operate a streaming service in the country. I expect the market to remain volatile until there is greater clarity and potential positive headlines from the ongoing trade negotiations. A strong Q4 earnings report by Netflix could provide the push the stock needs to start making the move higher.
Disclosure: I am/we are long NFLX, GOOGL. I wrote this article myself, and it expresses my own opinions. I am not receiving compensation for it (other than from Seeking Alpha). I have no business relationship with any company whose stock is mentioned in this article.
